Chapter 2 — Configuration

Configuration happens on the Panels DCC website in a browser — on your sofa, at a desk, or anywhere you have internet. You do not need to be next to the layout. When you are ready to run trains, PanelsDCC Control on the Raspberry Pi uses what you have set up here.

Everything is visual. There is no requirement to write scripts or edit configuration files. If you can click, type, and drag, you can add locomotives, accessories, and control panels.

Open Panels DCC website

Complete Getting started first (install, Wi‑Fi, Connect, first train, and your account) so Control can talk to your command station.

Recommended order

  1. Trains — add locomotives and their DCC numbers.
  2. Functions and function maps — icons for lights, horns, and other decoder features (optional until you want more than a basic throttle).
  3. Accessories — points, signals, and other layout items.
  4. Panels — draw the diagram you will operate from, and link it to those accessories.

Sensors, train detection, and route setting will be covered in later chapters. This chapter is the everyday setup path.

1. Trains

Your cloud library of locomotives, coaches, and wagons: pictures, status, DCC address, decoder notes, and function icons. Quick-add from the UK library, or enter details by hand.

Open Configuration — Trains

2. Accessories

Create points, colour-light and semaphore signals, crossings, and custom items. Each state has a DCC number. Macros group several accessories so you can set them together later in Control.

Open Configuration — Accessories

3. Panels

A panel is a control diagram of your layout — not a scale track plan. Place track, points, and signals, then link them to the accessories you have already created (or create a missing accessory without leaving the editor).

Open Configuration — Panels
